editor_note: None of the six rewritten entries (7, 14, 15, 16, 19, 23) would mislead a learner. They are faithful, and entry 16 ("Abgeschattete Lichtkegel", "Stichprobenaufwand") and entry 23 ("Quanten-Hamiltonoperatoren", "reduzierten Teilraum") read well. Entry 19 has two weak spots. It renders "Propagated noise absorption" as "Weitergeleitete Rauschabsorption", but the page uses "propagiert" elsewhere (entries 12 and 30), so it should be "Propagierte Rauschabsorption". It also uses neuter "ein Ziel-Observable", while the file otherwise uses feminine "die Observable(n)" (entries 16 and 18). Entry 7 has a small compound-hyphenation slip: "Qiskit Transpiler-Integration" should be "Qiskit-Transpiler-Integration".

editor_note: The rewritten heading [26] now reads "Dynamische Entkopplung". That is a correct and accepted German term, and the meaning has not drifted. The problem is that entry [24], the sentence that introduces this section, still says "Dynamical Decoupling" in English, and the sibling heading [27] keeps "Twirling" in English. The reader therefore meets two different names for the same technique a few lines apart. Either change the heading back to "Dynamical Decoupling" or change [24] to "dynamische Entkopplung" so the page uses one name.

examples.source: Dynamical Decoupling {#dynamical-decoupling}
examples.translation: Dynamische Entkopplung {#dynamical-decoupling}

editor_note: I checked the three rewritten entries (7, 8, 11) and none of them would mislead a learner. The 28-day window, the Flex Plan caveat, the 'known select error codes' and the two-instance example with double the minutes giving double the workloads all say the same thing as the English. Two spots are stiff, though. In entries 7 and 8, the Flex Plan note 'Das Fair-Share-Verhältnis … ist Gesamtnutzung im Verhältnis zur Zuweisung' has no article and doubles up on 'Verhältnis'. In entry 11, 'der doppelten Anzahl von Minuten … die doppelte Anzahl von Workloads' copies the English structure where German would say 'doppelt so viele'.

examples.source: The fair-share ratio for Flex Plan is total usage versus allocation.
examples.translation: Das Fair-Share-Verhältnis für den Flex Plan ist Gesamtnutzung im Verhältnis zur Zuweisung.
examples.suggested: Beim Flex Plan ist das Fair-Share-Verhältnis das Verhältnis von Gesamtnutzung zu Zuweisung.
examples.why: It has no article and says 'Verhältnis' twice, so it reads like a word-for-word translation of 'versus'. The same sentence appears again in entry 8.

examples.source: an instance with twice the number of minutes can execute twice the number of workloads.
examples.translation: kann eine Instanz mit der doppelten Anzahl von Minuten die doppelte Anzahl von Workloads ausführen.
examples.suggested: kann eine Instanz mit doppelt so vielen Minuten doppelt so viele Workloads ausführen.
examples.why: 'die doppelte Anzahl von' copies 'twice the number of'. 'doppelt so viele' is the natural German phrasing.

editor_note: None of the three rewritten entries (39, 56, 62) would mislead a learner. The defaults, the "replaces wholesale rather than merging" caveat, the 100 × 200 = 20,000 shots arithmetic and the one-tenth comparison are all correct. In entry 62, one "ergibt" governs both "20.000 Shots" and "etwa ein Zehntel der Circuit-Instanzen", so it reads as if the shot count produces the instance reduction. That clause should be restructured. Two smaller calques sit in the entry 39 table: "pro Site" should be "pro Gitterplatz", and "Entwickelt sich bis T" has no clear subject ("Entwickelt den Zustand bis T" is clearer).

examples.source: which is 20,000 shots per observable and about a tenth of the circuit instances the defaults would submit
examples.translation: was 20.000 Shots pro Observable ergibt und etwa ein Zehntel der Circuit-Instanzen, die die Standardwerte einreichen würden
examples.suggested: also 20.000 Shots pro Observable bei nur etwa einem Zehntel der Circuit-Instanzen, die mit den Standardwerten eingereicht würden
examples.why: One 'ergibt' covers both the shot total and the instance reduction, which is awkward. The meaning survives, but a native editor would split the two ideas.

examples.source: Evolves to `T = t_steps * dt` and reports every observable at each `t_k = k * dt`.

examples.why: The reflexive 'entwickelt sich' has no clear subject in the table cell, and 'meldet ... bei jedem t_k' copies the English syntax.

examples.source: per-site `Z`
examples.translation: pro Site `Z`
examples.suggested: `Z` pro Gitterplatz
examples.why: 'Site' is an English calque. German condensed-matter writing normally uses 'Gitterplatz'. The term is still recognizable, so this is minor.

editor_note: None of the nine rewritten entries would mislead a learner. The meaning is intact: client-side primitives and delegation to the Executor primitive (entry 5), "the only change is the import statement" (entry 6), and the Open Plan session caveat (entry 22). There are two small wording problems. Entry 6 renders "drop-in replacements" as "direkte Ersatzlösungen", which sounds stiff; a German developer would write "Drop-in-Ersatz". Entry 26 places the location phrase awkwardly after the clause in "Lerne, wie du lokal transpilierst, im Abschnitt [Transpile]". Terminology is consistent (Circuit, Observable, Transpiler, Sampler-Primitive) and the text uses "du" throughout.

examples.source: these client-side primitives are largely drop-in replacements of the legacy server-side primitives
examples.translation: sind diese clientseitigen Primitives größtenteils direkte Ersatzlösungen für die alten serverseitigen Primitives
examples.suggested: sind diese clientseitigen Primitives weitgehend ein Drop-in-Ersatz für die bisherigen serverseitigen Primitives
examples.why: 'direkte Ersatzlösungen' is a stiff, literal rendering; 'Drop-in-Ersatz' is the usual term in German developer writing, and 'bisherigen' fits 'legacy' better than 'alten'.

examples.source: Learn how to transpile locally in the [Transpile](transpile/) section.
examples.translation: Lerne, wie du lokal transpilierst, im Abschnitt [Transpile](transpile/).
examples.suggested: Im Abschnitt [Transpile](transpile/) lernst du, wie du lokal transpilierst.
examples.why: The location phrase comes after the embedded clause, copying the English word order, so the sentence reads awkwardly in German.

editor_note: The German is faithful and reads naturally in the "du" form. Terms are used the same way throughout (error mitigation→Fehlerminderung, error suppression→Fehlerunterdrückung, shots→Shots, noise model→Noise-Modell), and the caveat in [7] that a noise model goes stale is kept in "Beachte, dass ein Noise-Modell nach einer gewissen Zeit veraltet".

The translation is accurate and nothing in it would mislead a learner. The deprecation timeline in [3] (early 2025, removal in v2.0.0), the calibration-builder workflow in [5] and the fractional-gates flag caveat in [6] all match the English, and "fraktionale Gates" and "Pulssequenz" are used consistently. There is one grammar slip. In [5], "zum `target` eines QPU" gives QPU the wrong gender; German technical usage treats it as feminine (die QPU, after "die Recheneinheit"), so it should read "einer QPU".

examples.source: add either a `RXGate` or `RZXGate` instruction to a QPU's `target`

editor_note: None of the six rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entry 46 correctly reads "the hidden bitstring" as another name for "the correct answer", and entry 14's "ohne jede Konfiguration" is a fair rendering of "out of the box". A native editor would still change two things. First, entry 25's "in rekordbrechendem Maßstab" is a calque of "record-breaking scale". Second, several mixed English-German compounds lack the hyphens German spelling needs: "Fire Opal Pipeline-Methoden" (entry 14), "50-Qubit Quantum Kernel Learning" (entry 25) and "IBM Backends" (entry 32). Entries 8 and 35 are faithful, and "Circuit-Observable-Paares" is hyphenated correctly.

examples.translation: algorithmische Forschung in rekordbrechendem Maßstab ermöglicht
examples.suggested: algorithmische Forschung in bisher unerreichter Größenordnung ermöglicht
examples.why: 'rekordbrechend' is a direct calque of 'record-breaking'. It sounds off in German technical prose.

examples.line_approx: Alle Fire Opal Pipeline-Methoden sind vorkonfiguriert

examples.translation: Alle Fire Opal Pipeline-Methoden sind vorkonfiguriert

editor_note: Rewritten entries 6 and 13 are faithful and natural: "Basisvorlagen" matches heading [12], and "Sie sollen dir einen schnellen Einstieg in die Entwicklung ermöglichen" is an idiomatic rendering of "kickstart"; neither drops "original" in a way that changes the meaning, since "deiner eigenen" already carries it.

Neither rewritten entry changes the meaning of its source. Entry 3 is faithful and reads naturally: "Sampling von Quantenzuständen", "Berechnung von Erwartungswerten", and "Fehlerminderung" matches the cards in entries 5 and 7. Entry 9 has one spelling slip. The three link texts "EstimatorV2 API-Referenz", "SamplerV2 API-Referenz" and "Executor API-Referenz" leave a space inside a compound noun, which German spelling rules require to be hyphenated throughout ("EstimatorV2-API-Referenz"). Entry 9 uses the informal "du" correctly throughout ("Lerne", "Sieh dir … an", "Übe … durcharbeitest").

examples.source: See the [EstimatorV2 API reference](...), [SamplerV2 API reference](...), and [Executor API reference](...).
examples.translation: Lies die [EstimatorV2 API-Referenz](...), [SamplerV2 API-Referenz](...) und [Executor API-Referenz](...).
examples.suggested: Lies die [EstimatorV2-API-Referenz](...), [SamplerV2-API-Referenz](...) und [Executor-API-Referenz](...).

editor_note: None of the four rewritten entries (10, 12, 13, 18) changes the meaning. The quantities (33 qubits, 433 qubits, "fast viermal so groß") and the deprecation caveat in [18] match the English. There are two small editorial slips. "I/O" is spelled out as "Ein-/Ausgabeanforderungen" in [12] but kept as "I/O-Dichte" in the very next entry [13], so one form should be used in both. In [12], "wiring footprint" becomes "Verkabelungsbereich", which is vague; "footprint" means the space the wiring takes up, and "Platzbedarf der Verkabelung" would say that.

examples.source: to fit the greater I/O requirements within the same wiring footprint

examples.why: Entry [13] keeps 'I/O' ("I/O-Dichte"), so the two neighbouring entries spell the same term differently. 'Verkabelungsbereich' is also vaguer than 'footprint', which means the physical space taken up.

examples.source: allowing high-density I/O without sacrificing performance
examples.translation: was eine hohe I/O-Dichte ohne Leistungseinbußen ermöglichte
examples.suggested: (keep; align entry 12 to 'I/O')

editor_note: Both rewritten entries are accurate, and neither would mislead a learner. Entry 8, "Dynamical Decoupling", keeps the English technique name with German noun capitalization, which is a defensible choice. Entry 9, "Pauli Twirling", uses an open compound. German spelling rules join a compound that contains a proper name with a hyphen ("Pauli-Twirling", like "Pauli-Operator" and "Pauli-Matrix"), so a native editor would add the hyphen.

examples.source: [Pauli twirling](https://docs.quantum.ibm.com/api/qiskit-ibm-runtime/options-models-twirling-options)
examples.translation: [Pauli Twirling](https://docs.quantum.ibm.com/api/qiskit-ibm-runtime/options-models-twirling-options)

examples.why: In German, a compound with a proper name takes a hyphen (Pauli-Operator, Pauli-Gatter). The open form "Pauli Twirling" reads as an English calque and breaks German spelling rules.

editor_note: All six rewritten entries (6, 7, 15, 26, 34, 43) keep the English meaning. The caveats are intact: no noise modelling, statevector as the default, shot noise as opt-in, and `shots` at PUB level. The only thing a native editor would change is in the identical ISA tip sentence in entries 15 and 34. "Das Transpilieren des Circuits kann jedoch in Bezug auf die Circuit-Optimierung dennoch vorteilhaft sein" uses both "jedoch" and "dennoch", which says "however ... still" twice. "In Bezug auf" is also stiff. Keeping one of the two words and using a leaner phrasing would read more naturally.

examples.source: but transpiling the circuit might still be beneficial in terms of circuit optimization.
examples.translation: Das Transpilieren des Circuits kann jedoch in Bezug auf die Circuit-Optimierung dennoch vorteilhaft sein.
examples.suggested: Das Transpilieren des Circuits kann sich zur Circuit-Optimierung aber trotzdem lohnen.
examples.why: "jedoch" and "dennoch" together say "however" twice, and "in Bezug auf" is stiff, calqued phrasing. The meaning is correct.

examples.source: but transpiling the circuit might still be beneficial in terms of circuit optimization.
examples.translation: Das Transpilieren des Circuits kann jedoch in Bezug auf die Circuit-Optimierung dennoch vorteilhaft sein.
examples.suggested: Das Transpilieren des Circuits kann sich zur Circuit-Optimierung aber trotzdem lohnen.
examples.why: The same doubled "jedoch ... dennoch" as in entry 15. Fix both the same way so the two tip boxes stay identical.

editor_note: None of the five rewritten entries would mislead a learner. The meaning is faithful, including the 25-remainder-1 arithmetic in [16] and the experimental-option caveat in [20]. The problem is word choice. In headings [1]/[2], "Verzögerte Auflösung" renders "deferred" with the same word family the page uses for delay ("Verzögerung"), so it reads as "delayed" rather than "postponed", and it clashes with the title [0], which correctly says "aufzuschieben". Also, "löst sich zu einem Wert von 25 ... auf" in [16] is a calque, and "nachdem der Schaltkreis geplant wurde" in [20] is vague for "scheduled", where the rest of the page uses "Zeitplanung".

examples.source: Deferred timing resolution using stretch
examples.translation: Verzögerte Auflösung der Zeitangaben mit stretch
examples.suggested: Aufgeschobene Festlegung des Timings mit stretch
examples.why: This page uses 'Verzögerung' for delay, so 'verzögert' suggests a delay-related concept rather than postponement. It is also inconsistent with the title [0], which says 'aufzuschieben'. The same fix applies to heading [2].

examples.source: The above code resolves to a value of 25 with a remainder of 1.
examples.translation: Der obige Code löst sich zu einem Wert von 25 mit einem Rest von 1 auf.
examples.suggested: Für den obigen Code ergibt sich ein Wert von 25 mit einem Rest von 1.
examples.why: 'löst sich zu ... auf' is a calque of the English 'resolves to'. A code snippet does not 'dissolve' into a value in German.

examples.source: after the circuit is scheduled
examples.translation: nachdem der Schaltkreis geplant wurde
examples.suggested: nach der Zeitplanung (dem Scheduling) des Schaltkreises
examples.why: 'geplant' is vague: it could mean the circuit was designed. The rest of the page uses 'Zeitplanung' for scheduling, so that term should be used here too.

editor_note: None of the three rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entry 14 is faithful and reads naturally ("aufwändigere, aber auch rechenintensivere Optimierung"). In entry 50 the relative clause "der redundante Gates … entfernt" comes right after "anstelle von `CXCancellation`", so a German reader is likely to attach it to CXCancellation rather than CommutativeCancellation. The English "which" has the same ambiguity, but a native editor would move the clause next to the pass it describes. Entry 61 writes "Mehrqubit-Gates", while the rest of the file hyphenates as "Ein-/Zwei-/Drei-Qubit-Gates", so "Mehr-Qubit-Gates" would be consistent.

examples.source: this stage uses the CommutativeCancellation pass instead of CXCancellation, which removes redundant gates by exploiting commutation relations.
examples.translation: verwendet diese Phase den Pass [`CommutativeCancellation`](…) anstelle von `CXCancellation`, der redundante Gates durch Ausnutzung von Kommutationsrelationen entfernt.
examples.suggested: verwendet diese Phase anstelle von `CXCancellation` den Pass [`CommutativeCancellation`](…), der redundante Gates durch Ausnutzung von Kommutationsrelationen entfernt.
examples.why: Where the relative clause sits makes "der" seem to refer to CXCancellation. Moving it next to CommutativeCancellation makes clear which pass uses commutation relations.

examples.source: multi-qubit gate counts
examples.translation: Anzahl der Mehrqubit-Gates
examples.suggested: Anzahl der Mehr-Qubit-Gates
examples.why: The rest of the file hyphenates these compounds (Ein-Qubit-Gates, Zwei-Qubit-Gates, Drei-Qubit-Gate), so this one should match.

editor_note: None of the five rewritten entries would mislead a learner, but a native editor would still fix a few things. In [11], "und das falsche Bit wiederhergestellt wird" sits inside the wenn-clause, so the consequence reads like a second condition. In [46], "auf jedem der drei Qubits" can be read as "on each of the three qubits" instead of "any one", and "läuft das Ausführen … auf das Syndrom 00 hinaus" is stiff. In [23], "Workspace-Qubits" is an anglicism, and "CNOT-Gates (controlled-NOT)" does not match "kontrollierten-NOT-Gates" in [52]. Entries [7] and [51] are faithful and natural ("macht den Code blind für Bit-Flip-Fehler").

examples.source: then the decoding won't work properly and the wrong bit will be recovered
examples.translation: Natürlich wird das Dekodieren nicht korrekt funktionieren, wenn 2 oder 3 Bits der Kodierung umkippen, und das falsche Bit wiederhergestellt wird
examples.suggested: Natürlich funktioniert das Dekodieren nicht korrekt, wenn 2 oder 3 Bits der Kodierung umkippen – dann wird das falsche Bit wiederhergestellt.
examples.why: Because of the clause structure, 'wrong bit recovered' reads like part of the condition, not the result.

examples.source: a phase-flip error on any one of the three qubits ... running the error detection circuit from before on the state ... is certain to result in the syndrome 00
examples.translation: ein Phasen-Flip-Fehler auf jedem der drei Qubits ... Insbesondere läuft das Ausführen des Fehlererkennungsschaltkreises von zuvor auf dem Zustand ... mit Sicherheit auf das Syndrom $00$ hinaus
examples.suggested: ein Phasen-Flip-Fehler auf einem beliebigen der drei Qubits ... Insbesondere liefert der Fehlererkennungsschaltkreis von vorhin, angewendet auf den Zustand ..., mit Sicherheit das Syndrom $00$
examples.why: 'auf jedem' is ambiguous (each vs. any one), and the nominalized 'läuft das Ausführen … hinaus' is stiff translationese.

examples.source: two initialized workspace qubits and two controlled-NOT gates
examples.translation: zwei initialisierte Workspace-Qubits und zwei CNOT-Gates (controlled-NOT)
examples.suggested: zwei initialisierte Hilfsqubits (Arbeitsqubits) und zwei CNOT-Gates
examples.why: 'Workspace-Qubits' is an unneeded anglicism. The CNOT rendering also differs from 'kontrollierten-NOT-Gates' in entry 52.

editor_note: All four rewritten entries (2, 23, 35, 38) keep the meaning of the English and none would mislead a learner: the commute/anti-commute logic in [23], the (+1,+1) code-space claim in [35] and the X⊗X⊗X logical-X example in [38] all come through intact. Entry [35] renders 'code space' as '*Koderaum*', which clashes with the 'Code' spelling used everywhere else in the file (Wiederholungscode, Stabilisator-Code); the usual German term is 'Coderaum'. The participle phrase 'entsprechend den vier möglichen Syndromen' in [35] also reads stiffly. Entry [2] has 'Als nächstes', which current German spelling writes as 'Als Nächstes'. In [38] the nuance of 'turn out to' ('sich herausstellen') is dropped, which is a small loss of emphasis but not a change in meaning.

examples.source: which is the space of valid encodings (also known as the *code space*)
examples.translation: der Raum der gültigen Kodierungen (auch als *Koderaum* bekannt)
examples.suggested: der Raum der gültigen Kodierungen (auch als *Coderaum* bekannt)
examples.why: 'Koderaum' is not the usual German term and clashes with the 'Code' spelling used throughout the file. 'Coderaum' is the standard QEC term.

examples.source: The four 2-dimensional subspaces corresponding to the four possible syndromes are easy to describe
examples.translation: Die vier 2-dimensionalen Teilräume entsprechend den vier möglichen Syndromen lassen sich ... leicht beschreiben
examples.suggested: Die vier 2-dimensionalen Teilräume, die den vier möglichen Syndromen entsprechen, lassen sich ... leicht beschreiben
examples.why: A participle phrase placed after the noun is a stiff calque. A relative clause is what a native technical writer would use.

examples.source: Next, we'll take a second look
examples.translation: Als nächstes werfen wir einen zweiten Blick
examples.suggested: Als Nächstes werfen wir einen zweiten Blick
examples.why: Current German spelling rules capitalize 'Nächstes' when it is used as a noun.

editor_note: The rewritten entry 23 ("was sich bequem annähern lässt als") gives the sentence a second verb. Entry 25 already ends it with "approximiert werden kann, wenn N groß wird", so the rendered page reads "was sich bequem annähern lässt als [Formel] approximiert werden kann", which is ungrammatical. "sich annähern lässt als" is also unidiomatic German. The meaning (θ is approximately 1/√N for large N) still comes through, so this does not mislead. Entry 23 should only set up the verb that entry 25 supplies, for example "was sich bequem durch".

examples.source: which can be conveniently approximated as
examples.translation: was sich bequem annähern lässt als
examples.suggested: was bequem durch
examples.why: Entry 25 continues with "approximiert werden kann, wenn N groß wird", so this rewrite gives the sentence two predicates ("annähern lässt ... approximiert werden kann"). "sich annähern lässt als" is also not idiomatic. With "was bequem durch", the sentence reads "was bequem durch θ ≈ 1/√N approximiert werden kann, wenn N groß wird."

editor_note: None of the three rewritten entries (6, 13, 21) would mislead a learner. They keep the meaning, including the "kein Promise-Problem" negation, the "genau eine Lösung" promise, O(√N) and the "(sofern eine existiert)" caveat, and the file uses "Grovers Algorithmus" and "Überlagerung" consistently. One phrase is stiff: in entry 13, "verschachtelt diese Auswertungen mit anderen Operationen" is an awkward calque of "intersperses", and "wechselt … ab" reads more naturally. Entry 13 also drops "To be clear", which loses a little emphasis but no meaning.

examples.line_approx: Er wertet $f$ auf Überlagerungen … aus und verschachtelt diese Auswertungen
examples.source: intersperses these evaluations with other operations that have the effect of creating interference patterns
examples.translation: verschachtelt diese Auswertungen mit anderen Operationen, die Interferenzmuster erzeugen
examples.suggested: und wechselt diese Auswertungen mit anderen Operationen ab, die Interferenzmuster erzeugen
examples.why: 'verschachteln mit' is a stiff calque for 'intersperse'. 'abwechseln' says more naturally that the evaluations and the other operations alternate.

editor_note: Entries 4 and 138 are faithful and read naturally, for example "auf die Ordnungsbestimmung reduzieren", "Orthonormalsystem" and "gleichmäßig zufällig gewählt". Entry 159 leaves its second sentence unfinished. "Das bedeutet, dass N das Produkt" runs into the math block and never gets the verb "ohne Rest teilt", and entry 161 does not supply it either (compare 155/157, where "betrachten." is carried over). The German page therefore never actually states that N divides (a^{r/2}+1)(a^{r/2}-1). Entry 117 renders "figure out how to proceed" as "wie wir ohne ihn auskommen" ("how we manage without it"), which gives away the next step. It does not mislead the reader, but it is looser than the English.

examples.source: That means that $N$ evenly divides the product
examples.translation: Das bedeutet, dass $N$ das Produkt
examples.suggested: Das bedeutet, dass $N$ das folgende Produkt ohne Rest teilt:
examples.why: The verb is dropped and the next entry (161) does not supply it, so the German sentence is a fragment and never states the divisibility claim that the factoring argument depends on.

examples.source: so we need to figure out how to proceed.
examples.translation: wir müssen also herausfinden, wie wir ohne ihn auskommen.
examples.suggested: wir müssen also überlegen, wie wir weiter vorgehen.
examples.why: It adds an interpretation that is not in the source (managing without the eigenvector). This is accurate given what follows, but a native editor would keep the neutral wording.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. Nothing misleads: the petri-dish analogy, the caveat that the query model is "starr und künstlich", and the claim that Simon's algorithm gives a more robust advantage all come through intact. The slips are small. In [8], "führt einige kanonische Beispiele ... durch" reads as "carries out examples" when the English means "walks through" them. In [7], the German drops the reader ("führt John Watrous durch den Inhalt" has no "dich"), and the slide-download link sentence is a stiff calque. "Deutschs Algorithmus" and "Simons Algorithmus" are acceptable, but German texts usually write "Deutsch-Algorithmus" and "Simon-Algorithmus", which would also match "Deutsch-Jozsa-Algorithmus".

examples.source: steps through some canonical examples from quantum computing
examples.translation: führt einige kanonische Beispiele aus dem Quantencomputing durch
examples.suggested: geht einige kanonische Beispiele aus dem Quantencomputing durch
examples.why: 'durchführen' means to carry out or perform, not to walk through. 'durchgehen' is the right verb here.

examples.source: John Watrous steps you through the content ... [Download the slides] for this lesson.
examples.translation: führt John Watrous durch den Inhalt ... [Folien herunterladen] für diese Lektion.
examples.suggested: führt dich John Watrous durch den Inhalt ... Die [Folien zu dieser Lektion](...) kannst du hier herunterladen.
examples.why: The German leaves out the addressed reader ('dich'), and the link sentence copies the English word order, which sounds stiff in German.

examples.source: *Deutsch's algorithm* ... *Simon's algorithm*
examples.translation: *Deutschs Algorithmus* ... *Simons Algorithmus*
examples.suggested: *Deutsch-Algorithmus* ... *Simon-Algorithmus*
examples.why: German texts usually write these as compounds, which would also match the file's own 'Deutsch-Jozsa-Algorithmus'. The genitive form is still easy to recognize.

editor_note: None of the three rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entry 42 keeps the no-signalling argument intact ("zwingt Bob nichts dazu … aber es spricht auch nichts dagegen", "überlichtschneller Kommunikation"). Entry 49 ("eindeutig bestimmte Familie von Vektoren") is faithful, and entry 80 renders "unit trace" correctly as "die Spur 1 haben". A native editor would still change two small things. In entry 42, "aber das stimmt nicht wirklich" reads as the hedge "not quite true", while the English "this is not actually so" is a firm denial. In entry 80, the qualifier "for instance" was dropped, which makes computing ρ_A read as the goal rather than one example, since ρ_B is computed the same way in the next entry.

examples.source: …relies on the assumption that Bob has measured his qubit, but this is not actually so.
examples.translation: …auf der Annahme beruht, dass Bob sein Qubit gemessen hat, aber das stimmt nicht wirklich.
examples.suggested: …auf der Annahme beruht, dass Bob sein Qubit gemessen hat – das ist aber tatsächlich nicht der Fall.
examples.why: In German, 'stimmt nicht wirklich' is a hedge meaning 'not quite true'. The English is a firm denial, so the colloquial phrasing slightly weakens the point being made.

examples.source: To compute the reduced state $\rho_{\mathsf{A}}$ for instance, we can use linearity…
examples.translation: Um den reduzierten Zustand $\rho_{\mathsf{A}}$ zu berechnen, können wir Linearität…
examples.suggested: Um beispielsweise den reduzierten Zustand $\rho_{\mathsf{A}}$ zu berechnen, können wir die Linearität…
examples.why: The qualifier 'for instance' was dropped, even though the next entry computes ρ_B the same way. Adding the article ('die Linearität') also reads more naturally.

editor_note: None of the nine rewritten entries would mislead a learner. The scarf analogy (53), the probability/coin passage (49), 'destruktive Interferenz' (55) and the key takeaways (76, 81) all keep their meaning and caveats. Three spots still read like stiff, calqued German. Entry 53 has the clumsy 'auch wenn, wenn sie sich trennen würden'. Entry 21 carries over 'modify' as 'modifizierten das Wort „Computing"', which reads as a calque. Entry 15 ends with an awkward double 'vor' ('Stell dir … vor und nach … vor').

examples.source: the state of the two friends holding something purple is definite, even though, if separated, it is not known which friend would be holding the blue scarf
examples.translation: ist der Zustand der zwei Freunde, die etwas Lila halten, klar – auch wenn, wenn sie sich trennen würden, nicht bekannt wäre, welcher Freund den blauen Schal … halten würde
examples.suggested: ist der Zustand „zwei Freunde halten etwas Lila“ eindeutig – auch wenn man nicht wüsste, wer nach einer Trennung den blauen und wer den roten Schal hielte
examples.why: The stacked 'auch wenn, wenn' is clumsy calqued syntax. 'eindeutig' also fits 'definite' better than 'klar'.

examples.source: The words “classical” and “quantum” came to modify the word “computing” because this is how scientists already modified the word “physics,”
examples.translation: Die Wörter „klassisch" und „Quanten-" modifizierten das Wort „Computing", weil Wissenschaftler das Wort „Physik" bereits auf diese Weise nutzten
examples.suggested: Man stellte dem Wort „Computing“ die Zusätze „klassisch“ und „Quanten-“ voran, weil Wissenschaftler das Wort „Physik“ schon genauso näher bestimmten
examples.why: 'modifizierten' is a literal carry-over of 'modify', and 'auf diese Weise nutzten' does not quite match 'modified'. It reads as translationese.

examples.source: Consider the art and technique of photography before and after the advent of color film.
examples.translation: Stell dir die Kunst und Technik der Fotografie vor und nach der Erfindung des Farbfilms vor.
examples.suggested: Denk an die Kunst und Technik der Fotografie vor und nach der Erfindung des Farbfilms.
examples.why: Having 'vor … vor' next to each other is awkward. 'Denk an' or 'Betrachte' reads more naturally.

editor_note: None of the six rewritten entries changes the meaning. The optimization-level explanation (24), the session queueing claim (34) and the Estimator 0/1 and skip_transpilation rationale (36) all match the English, and du-register holds throughout. Two small editorial slips remain. Entry 34 copies the English "important enough that" as "wichtig genug, dass", where idiomatic German says "so wichtig, dass". Entry 36 writes "mit dem Pass Manager" without a hyphen, while entry 25 on the same page uses "Pass-Manager".

examples.source: These tools are important enough that we include a brief review of each
examples.translation: Diese Werkzeuge sind wichtig genug, dass wir jedes davon und seine Bedeutung für VQE kurz zusammenfassen
examples.suggested: Diese Werkzeuge sind so wichtig, dass wir jedes davon und seine Bedeutung für VQE kurz vorstellen
examples.why: 'wichtig genug, dass' copies the English structure word for word. Idiomatic German uses 'so wichtig, dass'.

examples.source: using the pass manager above
examples.translation: mit dem Pass Manager transpiliert haben
examples.suggested: mit dem Pass-Manager transpiliert haben
examples.why: Entry 25 on the same page writes 'Pass-Manager' with a hyphen, which is the correct German compound spelling. This entry drops the hyphen, so the file is inconsistent.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, the "du" register holds, and nothing would mislead a learner. For example, "Quantendiagonalisierung", "Skalierung von Ansätzen mit klassischen und Quantenalgorithmen" and the exam/Credly passages are all correct. The one thing a native editor would fix is the genitive of the neuter noun "Badge" in entry [16]. "zum Einlösen des Badge" and "Ausstellung deines Badge" are missing the genitive -s and should read "des Badges" and "deines Badges".

examples.source: You will receive an email notification from Credly with instructions for claiming the badge. Your personal information is used to issue your badge
examples.translation: mit Anweisungen zum Einlösen des Badge. Deine persönlichen Daten werden zur Ausstellung deines Badge sowie
examples.suggested: mit Anweisungen zum Einlösen des Badges. Deine persönlichen Daten werden zur Ausstellung deines Badges sowie
examples.why: "das Badge" is neuter and takes the strong genitive "des Badges". Leaving off the -s is a grammar slip that native readers will notice.

editor_note: I found no semantic drift. The tricky passages keep their meaning, including the p→1 dephasing subtlety [227], ZZ commutation propagation [265], [270], and the XY-vs-Z shrinkage in [205]. The file's terminology is split into blocks, apparently by translation batch. It uses "Circuit"/"Gate" in [11]–[73], switches to "Schaltkreis"/"Gatter"/"Quantengatter" in [75]–[111], mixes "Gates" with "Schaltkreis" in [237]–[282], and returns to "Circuit" in [284]–[295]. The classical-electronics section also calls electrical circuits "Circuit"/"integrierte Circuits" [11], [13], [19], where German uses "Schaltung". Other pairs also alternate: "Überdrehung"/"Überrotation", "Präparation"/"Vorbereitung", "Hamilton-Operator"/"Hamiltonian" and "Fidelity des Auslesens"/"Genauigkeit (Fidelity)".

examples.source: This means the resistance in the circuit can vary.
examples.translation: Das bedeutet, dass der Widerstand im Circuit variieren kann.
examples.suggested: Das bedeutet, dass der Widerstand in der Schaltung variieren kann.
examples.why: This is a classical electrical circuit, where the standard German term is 'Schaltung'. The English loanword 'Circuit' is reserved for quantum circuits and sounds wrong here. The same problem appears in [13] 'Circuit-Elementen' and [19] 'integrierten Circuits'.

examples.source: The error in the real circuit was fairly well described by the over/under-rotation error model.
examples.translation: Der Fehler im realen Schaltkreis wurde vom Über-/Unterdrehungs-Fehlermodell recht gut beschrieben.
examples.suggested: Der Fehler im realen Circuit wurde vom Über-/Unterrotations-Fehlermodell recht gut beschrieben.
examples.why: The file renders the same terms differently in different parts: 'Circuit' in [45] and [285] but 'Schaltkreis' here, 'Gate' in [73] but 'Gatter' in [75]–[111], and 'Überdrehung' here but 'Überrotation' in [237]. Pick one convention per term and use it throughout.

examples.source: a drive on qubit C "leaks through" into the Hamiltonian of qubit T
examples.translation: „sickert“ ein Drive auf Qubit C in den Hamiltonian von Qubit T durch
examples.suggested: „sickert“ ein Drive auf Qubit C in den Hamilton-Operator von Qubit T durch
examples.why: [119] uses the standard German term 'Hamilton-Operator', but here and in [253] the English 'Hamiltonian' appears. The term is inconsistent within the file.

examples.source: Perhaps surprisingly, a Z error on the target does cause an error to be propagated back to the control!
examples.translation: Überraschenderweise verursacht ein Z-Fehler am Ziel tatsächlich eine Ausbreitung eines Fehlers zurück zur Kontrolle!
examples.suggested: Vielleicht überraschend: Ein Z-Fehler am Ziel breitet sich tatsächlich zurück zur Kontrolle aus!
examples.why: The English hedge 'perhaps' is dropped, so the claim sounds stronger than the original. The nominal phrase 'verursacht eine Ausbreitung eines Fehlers' is also stiff.

examples.source: state preparation and measurement errors (or SPAM errors, for short)
examples.translation: die Zustandsvorbereitungs- und Messfehler (kurz: SPAM-Fehler)
examples.suggested: Zustandspräparations- und Messfehler (kurz: SPAM-Fehler)
examples.why: Most of the file uses the physics term 'präparieren/Präparation' ([48], [52], [262]), but the SPAM section switches to 'Vorbereitung'. The meaning is still clear, but the term is inconsistent.

editor_note: None of the 13 rewritten entries changes the meaning. The superposition caveat (23), the single-shot answers (28, 30) and the noise and queue points (39, 52) all match the English, and the terms are consistent (Gate, Circuit, Shots, Verschränkung, Kontroll-/Ziel-Qubit). Entry 31 says "Wenn du eine 0 misst, wird die andere auch 0 sein", which drops "one (qubit)", so "die andere" has nothing to refer to. Entry 44 uses the calque "ohne Vorkommnisse von 01 oder 10". In entry 54 the relative clause "der den Bell-Zustand erzeugt, wiederholtes Sampling verwendet und ... visualisiert" grammatically makes the circuit the one that does the sampling and visualizing, when "we" did.

examples.source: if you measure one to be 0, the other will be 0 and if you measure one to be 1, the other will also be 1
examples.translation: Wenn du eine 0 misst, wird die andere auch 0 sein, und wenn du eine 1 misst, wird die andere auch 1 sein.
examples.suggested: Wenn du bei einem Qubit eine 0 misst, liefert auch das andere eine 0, und wenn du bei einem eine 1 misst, liefert auch das andere eine 1.
examples.why: The qubit being measured is missing, so 'die andere' has no noun to refer to. The gender is also wrong for Qubit (das).

examples.source: with no occurrences of $01$ or $10$
examples.translation: ohne Vorkommnisse von $01$ oder $10$
examples.suggested: ohne ein einziges $01$ oder $10$
examples.why: 'Vorkommnisse' means incidents or events. It is a literal calque of 'occurrences'.

examples.source: We then built a simple two-qubit circuit that produces the $\Phi^+$ Bell state and used repeated sampling and visualized the entanglement
examples.translation: Anschließend haben wir einen einfachen Zwei-Qubit-Circuit erstellt, der den $\Phi^+$ Bell-Zustand erzeugt, wiederholtes Sampling verwendet und die Verschränkung ... visualisiert.
examples.suggested: Anschließend haben wir einen einfachen Zwei-Qubit-Circuit erstellt, der den $\Phi^+$ Bell-Zustand erzeugt. Mit wiederholtem Sampling haben wir die Verschränkung als Korrelation im Messhistogramm der Qubits sichtbar gemacht.
examples.why: The coordinated verbs get pulled into the relative clause, so the sentence reads as if the circuit did the sampling and visualizing, not us.

editor_note: All three rewritten entries mean what the English says and read naturally. Entry 6 ("Lade das PDF … herunter", "veraltet sein könnten") uses du and keeps the caveat. In entry 20, $|01\rangle$ still points to the position of the value 2. Entry 30 uses "Phaseninvertierung … über Phasen-Kickback", which matches the "Invertierung seiner Phase" wording in entry 14.

Nothing here would mislead a learner, but a few spots need an editor's touch. In [4], 'potential power of quantum computing' became 'potenziellen Nutzens' (usefulness, not power), and 'Grover's Algorithmus' uses an English possessive apostrophe where German would say 'Grover-Algorithmus'. In [8], 'Good-faith estimates' became the odd 'ehrliche Schätzungen', and in [9], 'in achieving useful quantum computing' became 'beim Einstieg in' (getting started), which weakens the goal. The du-register and 'Utility-Maßstab' are used consistently throughout.

examples.source: important to our understanding of the potential power of quantum computing
examples.translation: wichtig für das Verständnis des potenziellen Nutzens von Quantencomputern
examples.suggested: wichtig für das Verständnis der potenziellen Leistungsfähigkeit von Quantencomputern
examples.why: 'Power' means computational capability here, not usefulness; the shift is small but changes the emphasis.

examples.source: famous algorithms like Grover's and quantum phase estimation
examples.translation: bekannte Algorithmen wie Grover's Algorithmus und Quantum Phase Estimation
examples.suggested: bekannte Algorithmen wie den Grover-Algorithmus und die Quantenphasenschätzung (Quantum Phase Estimation)
examples.why: An English-style possessive apostrophe is non-standard in German; 'Grover-Algorithmus' is the usual term.

examples.source: Good-faith estimates of required QPU time have been provided
examples.translation: Am Anfang jeder Lektion wurden ehrliche Schätzungen der benötigten QPU-Zeit angegeben
examples.suggested: Am Anfang jeder Lektion findest du eine nach bestem Wissen erstellte Schätzung der benötigten QPU-Zeit
examples.why: 'ehrliche Schätzungen' is a literal calque of 'good-faith' and sounds odd; 'nach bestem Wissen' is the idiomatic German.

examples.source: useful to you and your students in achieving useful quantum computing
examples.translation: hilfreich beim Einstieg in nützliches Quantencomputing
examples.suggested: dabei helfen, nützliches Quantencomputing zu erreichen
examples.why: 'Einstieg' (getting started) turns the stated goal of achieving useful quantum computing into merely getting started.

editor_note: Entries 34 and 71 are faithful and read naturally: "Circuit-Synthese, die die Kopplungsbeschränkungen berücksichtigt" is a good rendering of "coupling constraint-aware", and "Wie du sehen kannst" keeps the du register. Entry 36 drops the qualifier "happens to". The source's "Qiskit transpiler happens to have no functions of synthesizing GHZ ..." presents the missing GHZ synthesis as a gap that exists now. The German "Der Qiskit-Transpiler bietet keine Funktionen ..." states it as a flat fact. This would not mislead a learner, but a word like "derzeit" would bring the original sense back.

examples.source: Qiskit transpiler happens to have no functions of synthesizing GHZ state preparation circuit.
examples.translation: Der Qiskit-Transpiler bietet keine Funktionen zur Synthese von GHZ-Zustandspräparations-Circuits.
examples.suggested: Der Qiskit-Transpiler bietet derzeit keine Funktion zur Synthese von GHZ-Zustandspräparations-Circuits.
examples.why: Dropping 'happens to' turns a gap that exists now into a flat, permanent-sounding statement. This is a small dropped qualifier and does not mislead.

editor_note: None of the four rewritten entries (11, 94, 107, 137) would mislead a learner. Entries 94, 107 and 137 are faithful, and "Wähle das Backend mit der kürzesten Warteschlange" is a good idiomatic rendering. Entry 11 has three small slips. The list heading "Superdense Coding (Quantum-Superdense-Coding)" adds a clumsy, redundant half-English gloss, while the rest of the file just says "Superdense Coding". "quantentechnisches Problem" reads as engineering rather than "quantum problem". "Information austauschen" softens "sending information" into a two-way exchange.

examples.source: **Quantum superdense coding**
examples.translation: **Superdense Coding (Quantum-Superdense-Coding)**
examples.suggested: **Superdense Coding**
examples.why: The parenthetical is a redundant half-English gloss that adds nothing. Headings 112 and 137 in the same file just say "Superdense Coding".

examples.source: To solve any utility-scale quantum problem, we will need to move information around
examples.translation: Um ein quantentechnisches Problem im Utility-Maßstab zu lösen, müssen wir in der Lage sein, Information ... zu bewegen
examples.suggested: Um ein Quantenproblem im Utility-Maßstab zu lösen, müssen wir Information ... von einem Qubit zu einem anderen übertragen
examples.why: "quantentechnisch" suggests quantum engineering, not a quantum computing problem. "in der Lage sein" is extra padding the English doesn't have.

examples.source: such as "distant friends sending information"
examples.translation: etwa „entfernte Freunde, die Information austauschen"
examples.suggested: etwa „entfernte Freunde, die einander Information senden"
examples.why: "austauschen" implies a two-way exchange, but the protocols are one-way sends. This is a small nuance shift, not a misleading one.

editor_note: None of the 60 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. The x_i/z_i mapping (65), the cut-indicator condition (43), the dropped 1/4 factor and n^2 offset (69) and the 'not optimal due to noise, optimum is 5' caveat (115) all match the English. The remaining issues are about fluency. 'Prepare a state' is calqued as 'Zustand vorbereiten' in 53, 74 and 107, where German physics writing uses 'präparieren'. In 107, 'kollabieren' is used transitively ('wird den Zustand ... kollabieren'), which is ungrammatical. In 13, the compound 'Fehlermitigation- und Fehlerunterdrückungstechniken' is missing its linking s, and 'im Utility-Scale' reads awkwardly.

examples.source: Create a quantum circuit which will prepare the ground state of this Hamiltonian
examples.translation: der den Grundzustand dieses Hamiltonoperators ... vorbereitet
examples.suggested: der den Grundzustand dieses Hamiltonoperators ... präpariert
examples.why: German physics uses 'einen Zustand präparieren'. 'Vorbereiten' is a literal calque. The same slip appears in 74 and 107.

examples.source: A measurement will collapse the state into a single computational basis state
examples.translation: Eine Messung wird den Zustand in einen einzelnen Rechenbasis-Zustand kollabieren
examples.suggested: Eine Messung lässt den Zustand in einen einzelnen Zustand der Rechenbasis kollabieren
examples.why: 'kollabieren' is intransitive in German, so it cannot take 'den Zustand' as an object.

examples.source: at a utility scale, thanks to the application of various error mitigation and suppression techniques
examples.translation: im Utility-Scale bereitzustellen, dank der Anwendung verschiedener Fehlermitigation- und Fehlerunterdrückungstechniken
examples.suggested: im Utility-Maßstab zu liefern, dank verschiedener Techniken zur Fehlermitigation und Fehlerunterdrückung
examples.why: The linking s is missing ('Fehlermitigations-'), and 'im Utility-Scale' is an awkward English-German hybrid.

editor_note: None of the five rewritten entries (11, 40, 42, 51, 58) would mislead a learner. The cut condition in [58] keeps the right sign (−1 means cut, 1 means not cut), and 'Fehlerminderungstechnik' in [51] matches entry [16]. Two spots still read like translated English. In [11], 'einen detaillierten Durchgang durch die Inhalte' is a literal copy of 'walkthrough'. In [40], 'ist das Finden eines guten Initial-Mappings eine herausfordernde Aufgabe' is stiff, and 'wurde auf bis zu 500 Qubits skaliert' loses a little of the English 'has been demonstrated to scale'.

examples.source: For a detailed walkthrough of the contents of this tutorial, see this [Qiskit video]
examples.translation: Für einen detaillierten Durchgang durch die Inhalte dieses Tutorials siehe dieses [Qiskit-Video]
examples.suggested: Eine ausführliche Erklärung der Inhalte dieses Tutorials findest du in diesem [Qiskit-Video].
examples.why: 'Durchgang durch die Inhalte' copies 'walkthrough' word for word. The suggested wording is more natural German and uses the informal 'du' address.

examples.source: finding a good initial mapping is a challenging task ... This approach has been demonstrated to scale to up to *500 qubits*
examples.translation: ist das Finden eines guten Initial-Mappings eine herausfordernde Aufgabe ... Dieser Ansatz wurde auf bis zu *500 Qubits* skaliert
examples.suggested: ist es schwierig, ein gutes Initial-Mapping zu finden ... Es wurde gezeigt, dass dieser Ansatz auf bis zu *500 Qubits* skaliert
examples.why: The noun phrase 'das Finden eines ...' and 'herausfordernde Aufgabe' are stiff. 'Wurde ... skaliert' also drops the idea of a demonstration from 'has been demonstrated', though 'wie im Paper dargestellt' partly makes up for it.

editor_note: Entry 64 is faithful and reads naturally. "EstimatorV2-Primitiv mit dem Fake-Backend", "AQC-optimierten Schaltkreis" and "Basis-Trotter-Schaltkreis" match the renderings in [62]/[66], and "die ZZ-Observable für jeden zu messen" keeps the per-circuit measurement.

All three rewritten entries keep the meaning, with no drift or hallucination. Entry 38 is clean: "variiert" for "sweeps" and "in einem einzigen Aufruf bei vielen Parameterwerten auswerten" match the English. There are two small issues a native editor would fix. In entry 7, the genitive "des EstimatorV2-Primitives" should be "Primitivs", since the noun is "das Primitiv" everywhere else on the page (entries 0, 38, 62). In entry 58, "Wo immer eine Kurve in die grauen Bänder eintritt" and "die Variation im Rauschen von Paar zu Paar" read like calques of the English. "Sinuswelle" is fine, but "Sinuskurve" would be more usual for a plotted curve.

examples.source: in a single call to the EstimatorV2 primitive
examples.translation: in einem einzigen Aufruf des [`EstimatorV2`](...)-Primitives berechnet
examples.suggested: in einem einzigen Aufruf des [`EstimatorV2`](...)-Primitivs berechnet
examples.why: The page uses the neuter noun 'das Primitiv', so its genitive is 'des Primitivs'. '-Primitives' is a hybrid of the English form and doesn't match entries 0 and 38.

examples.source: the spread between the faint curves reflects the variation in noise from pair to pair. Wherever a curve enters the grey bands, it has crossed the classical bound
examples.translation: die Streuung zwischen den blassen Kurven spiegelt die Variation im Rauschen von Paar zu Paar wider. Wo immer eine Kurve in die grauen Bänder eintritt, hat sie die klassische Grenze ... überschritten
examples.suggested: die Streuung zwischen den blassen Kurven spiegelt wider, wie stark das Rauschen von Paar zu Paar schwankt. Sobald eine Kurve in die grauen Bänder hineinreicht, hat sie die klassische Grenze ... überschritten
examples.why: 'Wo immer ... eintritt' and 'Variation im Rauschen' follow the English syntax closely. The meaning is correct, but a German technical writer would phrase it more idiomatically.

editor_note: Entries 12 and 71 are faithful. The noisy-channel direction (true j read as i) and the interleaving/unscramble order both match the English. In entry 82 the tenses split within one sentence: "war die dominierende Fehlerquelle" but "die M3-Mitigation wirksam ist". The English "was effective" is about this one experiment, and the present tense turns it into a slightly broader general claim, so both verbs should be in the past tense. A smaller point: in entry 12, "fälschlicherweise als $i$ gelesen" should be "ausgelesen", which is the verb the page uses for readout everywhere else.

examples.source: readout error was the dominant source of error and the M3 mitigation was effective.
examples.translation: der Auslesefehler die dominierende Fehlerquelle war und die M3-Mitigation wirksam ist.
examples.suggested: der Auslesefehler die dominierende Fehlerquelle war und die M3-Mitigation wirksam war.
examples.why: Tense mismatch within one sentence. The present tense 'ist' makes the result of one experiment sound like a general claim, which the English does not make.

examples.source: a true value of $j$ will be incorrectly read as $i$.
examples.translation: dass ein wahrer Wert von $j$ fälschlicherweise als $i$ gelesen wird.
examples.suggested: dass ein wahrer Wert $j$ fälschlicherweise als $i$ ausgelesen wird.
examples.why: The page uses 'Auslese/auslesen' for readout (for example entry 27, 'falsch ausgelesen'). The bare 'gelesen' sounds like a calque and 'von $j$' is awkward.

editor_note: The three rewritten entries (7, 34, 51) are faithful and read naturally, with no meaning drift: the once-daily updates, the within-day fluctuations, the stale-properties risk in the transpilation step, and the caveat that updated device information matters less as chain length grows ("wird die Bedeutung aktualisierter Geräteinformationen geringer") all come through, as do "transiente Zwei-Niveau-Systeme" and the du-register call to action.

The meaning holds throughout, including the long caveat about diagonal-term filtering in [59] and the subspace-dimension note in [84], and nothing would mislead a learner. The terminology changes partway through the page. "circuit" is "Circuit"/"Circuit-Tiefe" in [0]–[30] but "Schaltkreis"/"Schaltkreistiefe" from [47] on. "Hamiltonian" is "Hamiltonian" in [16]–[38] but "Hamiltonoperator" from [44] on. [47] also attaches "das … bereitstellt" to "Schaltkreismodell" rather than to qiskit-fermions and turns "transpiler passes" into "transpilerspezifische Passes". A few calques remain, such as "zu recovern" in [93] and "Zeitentwicklungszeiten" in [61]/[93].

examples.source: while also reducing the circuit depth
examples.translation: reduziert dabei gleichzeitig die Circuit-Tiefe
examples.suggested: Settle on one term for the whole file, either Circuit/Circuit-Tiefe or Schaltkreis/Schaltkreistiefe (from [47] on the page uses Schaltkreis)
examples.why: 'circuit' is rendered two ways in one file: Circuit in [0]-[30], Schaltkreis from [47] on.

examples.source: constructed directly from the target Hamiltonian
examples.translation: direkt aus dem Ziel-Hamiltonian konstruiert werden
examples.suggested: direkt aus dem Ziel-Hamiltonoperator konstruiert werden
examples.why: 'Hamiltonian' is kept in English in [16]-[38] and becomes 'Hamiltonoperator' from [44] on.

examples.source: using `qiskit-fermions`, which provides transpiler passes and gates specific to fermionic circuits
examples.translation: auf ein fermionisches Schaltkreismodell ab, das transpilerspezifische Passes und Gates für fermionische Schaltkreise bereitstellt
examples.suggested: … mit `qiskit-fermions`, das Transpiler-Passes und Gates speziell für fermionische Schaltkreise bereitstellt, auf ein fermionisches Schaltkreismodell ab.
examples.why: The relative clause now says the circuit model, not the library, provides the passes, and 'transpilerspezifisch' changes what the passes are.

examples.source: since it postselects rather than recovers
examples.translation: da er postselektiert statt zu recovern
examples.suggested: da er Postselektion statt Konfigurations-Recovery verwendet
examples.why: 'zu recovern' is Denglish that a native technical writer would not use.

examples.source: subsampling smaller time-evolution operators from the Hamiltonian based on its coefficients
examples.translation: indem kleinere Zeitentwicklungsoperatoren basierend auf ihren Koeffizienten aus dem Hamiltonian subgesampelt werden
examples.suggested: indem kleinere Zeitentwicklungsoperatoren anhand seiner Koeffizienten aus dem Hamiltonoperator gezogen werden
examples.why: 'ihren' points to the operators, but the coefficients belong to the Hamiltonian ('its'). 'subgesampelt' is also clumsy.
